q: A certificate is otherwise trusted but its SAN is web.example; should a client requesting api.example accept it?
expected: web.example differs from api.example in the leftmost label; hostname verification fails, so the connection must be rejected.

q: What happens when a first-match deny rule precedes a narrow allow for the very same packet tuple?
expected: 198.51.100.42 belongs to the denied /24, so rule 1 denies it before the exception can be evaluated.

q: Does removing one permitted cross-zone connection always isolate the third trust zone?
expected: Before blocking api→data, breadth-first reachability from user is {user,api,data,dns}, four nodes.

q: Can a 16,385-byte application message fit into a single TLS 1.3 plaintext fragment?
expected: For 16,385 bytes, ceil(16,385/16,384)=2 fragments, not one; 16,384 bytes fit exactly one under the bound.

q: Which operations should three roles receive when an explicit four-service allow matrix is evaluated?
expected: Across 3×4=12 role–service cells, exactly 4 are allowed and 8 denied; reader→admin is denied.

q: How does a TLS 1.3 record sequence number affect the per-record nonce within one key epoch?
expected: With an all-zero twelve-byte IV, sequence 0 gives nonce hex 000000000000000000000000; sequence 1 ends in 01.

q: Why is a trusted root alone insufficient to authenticate a certificate for the requested service?
expected: The simulated root check returns true but service-b.example is absent from the SAN list, so authenticated=false.

q: Can a stateful allow-outbound policy admit replies without admitting unsolicited inbound connections?
expected: Outbound SYN creates one table entry; reverse server:443→client:51000 is accepted, but server:443→client:51001 is dropped.

q: Which requests remain possible under a DNS-only cross-zone exception rather than a blanket allow?
expected: Of the three invented requests, exactly one matches the narrow policy; two fail the default-deny check.

q: What replay risk remains if a payment-like side effect is accepted from TLS 1.3 early data?
expected: The same synthetic request accepted twice increments the counter from 0 to 2, despite only one intended logical operation.

q: Can a matching certificate commonName compensate for a mismatched subjectAltName?
expected: The SAN comparison is false, so this request must fail identity validation even though the CN text happens to match.

q: Which of three boundary addresses belong to a documentary /24 CIDR allowlist?
expected: The first two candidates match the /24 bitmask; the third differs in the third octet and fails.

q: How much does one denied interzone hop reduce the modeled reachable resource set?
expected: Before blocking gateway→database, the client reaches five nodes; after blocking it, reachable count is four.

q: Does the RFC 5869 SHA-256 HKDF vector independently reproduce both extraction and expansion?
expected: The RFC test PRK begins 077709362c2e32df and the 42-byte OKM begins 3cb25f25faacd57a9043.

q: Which application protocol can be selected when client and server ALPN lists differ?
expected: The set intersection is {http/1.1}, so that is the sole possible selection under these offered lists.

q: Will default-deny egress permit an unlisted documentation host at the same destination port?
expected: Exactly two of the three requests match; the third host must be denied despite using TCP port 443.

q: Does routing between two VLAN-labeled zones automatically mean the trust boundary is enforced?
expected: With both edges present, management is reachable from employees in two hops; removing lab→management breaks that modeled path.

q: Does a correctly validated TLS server identity authorize every HTTP operation at that server?
expected: The simulated TLS identity gate passes, but viewer→delete-record is absent from the role matrix, so operation is denied.

q: What changes when a TLS service certificate is checked against an expired synthetic validity window?
expected: Although requested SAN app.example matches the presented identifier, Nov 11 occurs after June 30 so the mock is invalid.

q: Why is a reverse reply permitted only while a modeled outbound state entry exists?
expected: Before expiry, the resolver reply to client port 53000 matches; after expiry the same packet fails the state check.

q: Can a one-direction allow edge be assumed to permit the reverse flow in a trust graph?
expected: devices reaches archive in two hops; archive cannot reach devices by any directed path in this graph.

q: Should a TLS 1.3 key update continue the prior record counter and reuse the same record nonce?
expected: Sequence 0 in epoch A ends in nonce 00, whereas sequence 0 in epoch B ends in nonce 01 under our illustrative IVs.

q: Does a wildcard DNS SAN for *.example match both a.example and b.a.example?
expected: a.example matches the wildcard whereas b.a.example has two subdomain labels and fails.

q: Does an IPv4-only blocklist cover an IPv6 packet just because the application service is the same?
expected: The IPv4 packet matches the /24 deny, while the IPv6 documentation address misses the IPv4-only entry and is allowed in this model.
